title.narrative: Improved skills development strategies, policies and programmes for promoting the employability of young men and women

description.narrative: Despite a general decline in the overall unemployment rate, youth unemployment remains a significant concern. A particularly troubling trend is 20.31% of young people are neither employed, in education, nor in training (NEET). The ILO’s technical assistance aims to enhance skills, policies, and programs to improve employability for both young men and women. In this biennium, the ILO prioritizes strengthening the capacity development of social partners and providing policy advice to improve Indonesia's vocational training system, making it more responsive to private sector needs. This approach includes enhancing labour market information and services to boost employability and job access, particularly for youth, while simultaneously improving the vocational training system through competency-based training, certification, and the development of replicable training programs such as apprenticeships. The ILO places particular emphasis on inclusivity for women and persons with disabilities, ensuring that skills development initiatives address the diverse needs of Indonesia's workforce. The organization is conducting a study on skill development funds to explore innovative financing schemes for skill development in the country, alongside developing guidance on grievance mechanisms and quality internships. Additionally, the ILO supports the establishment of Sector Skill Committees in the shipbuilding and tourism sectors while conducting a work-based learning assessment in the electronics sector to ensure apprenticeships align with ILO quality standards. These integrated efforts focus on creating sustainable pathways from education to employment, bridging the skills gap between what industries require and what the current workforce can provide. The primary beneficiaries include social partners, institutions, and stakeholders involved in skills development and youth employment, ultimately contributing to a more skilled, inclusive, and employment-ready workforce.
